title: Mainnet settlement-side measurement of price-drift frequency (x402 issue #3866 comment)
quote: For 12 to 23 October 2026, at the 80 sellers with 20 or more settlements in the window (32,605 settlements, $18,950.78 in total), measured 2026-10-24T08:50Z: 1,126 settlements (3.5%) were at least 10 times the sellers own median settlement in the window; 65 were at least 100 times it; 25 of those were also at least $1. [Later in the same thread, after three independent fix implementations converged:] Thanks to everyone involved for two rounds of rigorous review, for the replay + expectedAmount sketch, for the honest doc-only mapping, for the third independent implementation and the provenance/anchor-integrity points, and for the mainnet settlement-side measurement (honestly framed as a ceiling, not evidence of exploitation). [TKCollective, disclosing a gap in their own x402-guard package found while reviewing PR #3920:] Our side. @tanilo/x402-guard 0.1.1 (disclosure: we build it) compared the declared amount against supplied terms, compared the recipient only when the terms entry named a payTo, and never compared asset or network. [NSPG13, reviewing PR #3920 itself:] Concurrent first calls: the ledgers are written only after await schemeNetworkClient.createPaymentPayload(...). Two calls on a fresh client can both pass the empty-ledger check and enter the signer before either anchor exists.

title: feat(core): expected-amount control in client spend controls — enforce caller price expectation pre-signature
quote: As established in #3866: a spending cap limits maximum exposure, but does not verify that the requested amount matches the callers intended price. This PR adds an expected-amount control to client-side spend controls: the callers price expectation is enforced at payment creation, before the signer is called.

title: [Bug]: Python register_exact_evm_client / register_exact_svm_client ignore networks for V1, so a testnet-only client still signs V1 mainnet payments
quote: a client that was explicitly limited to a testnet refuses a V2 offer on eip155:8453, but if the server answers with a V1 402 for base instead, the client signs a V1 authorization for Base mainnet. Same key, same funds, just a different x402Version in the 402. The TypeScript helpers already do the right thing: registerExactEvmScheme and registerExactSvmScheme filter the V1 network list by config.networks

title: feat(core,specs): enforce self-payment prohibition (payer !== payTo) and pre-signing group sponsor invariants
quote: x402Facilitator.verify() and x402Facilitator.settle() now reject payments where the payload or scheme-resolved payer equals paymentRequirements.payTo (case-insensitively normalized) with invalid_self_payment. Prevents circular self-settlement wash volume (payer === payTo, which transfers zero net economic value) and blocks settlement-gated catalog self-indexing abuse.

title: fix(python): reject settlement overrides above the authorized amount
quote: resolve_settlement_override_amount() accepted raw, percent, and dollar overrides that resolved above PaymentRequirements.amount. A 500% override of 1000000 atomic units returned 5000000... The resolver now raises ValueError when the resolved atomic amount is greater than that authorized maximum.

title: fix(go): enforce settlement override ceiling against PaymentRequirements.amount
quote: ResolveSettlementOverrideAmount now rejects a raw, percent, or dollar override when the resolved atomic amount is greater than PaymentRequirements.Amount. Partial settlement, including the upto scheme, returns invalid_settlement_override instead of forwarding an amount above the authorized maximum. This is the Go part of #3876 and leaves the Python port open.
